MWCC GC 1.2.5, -O4. EXTENSION of claim.law.BF_the-unfused-branch-pair-is-an-inlined-callee-return-not-any-return.20260903.v1 and claim.law.NM_branch-pair-fusion-is-blocked-by-a-return-not-by-a-goto.20260903.v2 PART 2, from six functions worked in one run (four closures, two refusals). THREE clauses, each measured both ways.

CLAUSE 1 -- THE LIFT'S UNSTATED PRECONDITION IS EXPANSION, AND IT IS NOT GUARANTEED BY `static inline`. The cure is 'the pair is an inlined callee's return', so it can only work if MWCC ACTUALLY INLINES the helper, and MWCC sometimes refuses. `powerpc-eabi-nm` on the built object is the whole decision procedure: a `t` symbol for the helper means it was outlined and every score you are reading describes a CALL, not an inline. Measured on four TUs all built with the same `cflags_demo`: EXPANDED (no symbol) in game/world/gauntworld.o (find_keyring_row), game/sfx/psfx.o (PlyrSfxWrapTime, PlayerFadeWeapTrail) and game/audio/audio.o (AudioFreeQueueSlot); REFUSED in game/game/player.o, where `player_level_for_exp` appears as `000064a4 t player_level_for_exp` and the function's whole loop leaves our stream (insns 161/170 ours/target against the baseline's 169/170, real 171 -> 175). Four spellings were measured at that one function -- helper inside the `#pragma dont_inline on` bracket, helper moved outside it, the `for(;;)`/`break` loop respelt as a counted `for`, and `#pragma always_inline on` around the helper -- and all four landed on the identical outlined 161/170. So the refusal is not the dont_inline pragma and not the loop spelling; the only structural difference from the three expanded helpers is that this one's loop body contains a real `bl` to a same-TU global (LevelToExp). CHECK NM BEFORE RECORDING ANY LIFT RESULT.

CLAUSE 2 -- v1's `if (A || B) { return; }` IS NOT SUPERSEDED BY THE INLINE-LIFT REFINEMENT; THEY ARE TWO TOOLS. On game/sfx/psfx PlayerDoWeapTrail the refinement's own cure was measured DEAD TWICE (both lifts landed at real 177, insns 137/140 ours/target, with the guard STILL folded to a single `beq` -- an early return at the TOP of an inline is not a merge point and carries no pair) while merging the function's two separate `if (...) { goto done; }` guards into one `if (player->activeNode == NULL || gFrameTicks == 0) { return; }` closed the pair on the first probe, taking the multiset 4t -> 1t. Try v1's guard-merge form FIRST when the site is a pair of function-scope guards, and reach for the lift when the site is a value join.

CLAUSE 3 -- THE RECOGNITION RULE IS NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT, AND THE SECOND SCREEN IS WHETHER AN INLINE CAN REACH THE SITE AT ALL. v2's rule (the pair's unconditional `b` lands on a block that assigns a value and falls through to its consumer) held for all four closures this run and screened OUT game/ui/screensaver ControllerMessageBox correctly, where the `b` is a loop back-edge. But it ALSO holds at two sites that did not close: game/game/player player_get_from_save (the `b` lands on `stw r28,13092(r29)` with `li r28,1` in the fallthrough) refused because of clause 1, and game/ui/select update_class_attr (the `b` lands on `stw r0,0(r4)` with `li r0,999` in the fallthrough) refused with the lift NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL -- the object did not move one byte, i.e. MWCC normalises the lift and the tree's existing empty-then-arm diamond to the same IR. On that second one the one-case switch is also dead here even though v1 records it working on update_class_spec 'because its arms assign a value': a BOOLEAN switch selector gets MWCC's branchless idiom (`eqv`/`subfc`/`srwi`/`addze`) and grew the function by 6 instructions.

TWO COROLLARIES worth carrying. (a) THE LIFT ALWAYS MOVES THE FRAME, in both directions: it orphans the outer function's locals (claim.law.dead-nominal-local-area-tracks-declaration-count.20260831.v1) AND adds the helper's own, so budget one probe for the frame every time -- PlyrSfxDoDamage needed the caller's now-unused `f32 frac;` deleted (real 175 -> 141, and every stack-offset immediate returned to the target's), fn_8005E90C needed its pad taken 16 -> 12 bytes (frame 80 -> 72 -> the target's 72, real 24 -> 14), and PlayerDoWeapTrail's first lift LOST 8 bytes of frame by moving every local out of the caller. (b) PASS LOOP BOUNDS BY POINTER, NOT BY VALUE. Passing fn_8005E90C's bound as `s32 count` hoisted the reload into the preheader (`lwz r24,116(r3)` at +0x1ac where the target reloads inside the loop at +0x1f0) and fresh fuzzy FELL 95.9407 -> 95.8296 even at real 52; passing the base pointer and leaving `*(s32*)(world + 116)` in the loop CONDITION took it to real 24 and fuzzy 96.8481, then real 14 after the frame fix.
